subject: Best practices for evaluating different specifications of the spatial component in lgcp?

messages.author: 067e97ce536c222f
messages.subject: Best practices for evaluating different specifications of the spatial component in lgcp?
parts:
Hello, 
I am working on some presence-only species distribution models and am getting some substantially different predictions of lambda based on the spatial smoothing component (e.g., using different max.edge lengths, altering the priors for for the inla.spde2.pcmatern specification, etc). My concern is that the spatial component is overfitting the data (evidenced by sharp drops in lambda just beyond the edge of the presence locations; see the attached image). I've tried using model selection based on a saturated model containing all of my covariates and different formulations of the spatial effect, but the "overfit" (i.e., the one with the tightly constrained spatial term model consistently outperforms models with 'smoother' spatial terms. This suggests to me that using the saturated model is, perhaps, not the best way to select the 'appropriate' formulation of inla.spde2.pcmatern. I've tried using the meshbuilder() mesh assessment tools (that's how I ended up using the 'overfit' specification for the mesh), but that seems to focus on the theoretical properties of the mesh (not the estimation of the random field based on the mesh AND priors).I'm wondering whether others have a reference or "best practice" for choosing among competing formulations of the spatial component? Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.
Best,
Matt Williamson
